newsitem.title: ITALY: Magneti stock rises after Brazil Cofap buy.
newsitem.headline: Magneti stock rises after Brazil Cofap buy.

text.p: Magneti Marelli, the Italian vehicle component maker controlled by Fiat, firmed on the Milan bourse following news it was buying 70 percent of the voting capital in Brazil's Cofap, the leading South American auto components company.
Analysts said the move reinforced Magneti's leadership in the South American market and particularly the spare parts sector where Magneti wants to expand to grow its margins.
Magneti announced the purchase on Friday without putting a figure on the value of the deal.
Magneti stock closed 3.24 percent up at 2,870 lire after a session high at 2,935, in volume of over one million shares. The Milan bourse ended over 1.5 percent lower.

"The deal's been done in a market where car sales should show rises of eight to 10 percent, despite some worries linked to a hike in the tax on financial operations," said Fabrizio Gastaldi of Centrosim securities house which confirmed its long-term buy recommendation for the stock.

Elena Sottanella of Pasfin confirmed its buy, noting that the deal reinforced Magneti's presence in South America. She added that Cofap was reported to have a Return on Sales ratio of around 6.9 percent.
"We reckon Magneti will have to pay something like 250 to 300 billion lire for the stake," she said.
Gianni Allavena, head of research at Intersim recommended an accumulate and thought reasonable a Magneti target share price of 3,500 lire on the basis of good 1998 results.

"The operation is strategically positive even if the price is not known. Some 30 percent of Cofap turnover comes from the 'aftermarket' where Magneti is fairly weak and where the margins are particularly interesting," he said.
"This purchase makes clearer Magneti's goal of growing margins and doubling its share of the aftermarket by 2000," he said.
